extracted.intended_audience: research teams and faculty preparing FY25 MURI white papers and full proposals for DoD (ONR/ARO/AFOSR) funding
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare a multidisciplinary white paper/full proposal responding to one of the FY25 MURI topic descriptions (objectives, research concentration areas, and resource expectations) for ONR/ARO/AFOSR. The page lists per-topic objectives, suggested research concentration areas, anticipated resources, and special participation/funding notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective: study materials properties using quantum simulators
rubrics_metrics.description: The objective of this MURI is to study materials properties at the microscopic level using quantum simulator platforms and model systems implemented on them to gain new fundamental insights into the mechanical, thermal, and/or vibrational behavior of materials. A secondary objective is to use quantum simulator platforms to accelerate the iterative process of identifying and designing new materials with physical properties of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should emphasize investigations beyond purely electronic/spintronic/optoelectronic/photonic behaviors; show how quantum simulators can benchmark and improve computational techniques and accelerate materials design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Concentration Area: theoretical approaches for materials design
rubrics_metrics.description: Theoretical approaches (computational and analytical) to design real or model materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes inverse design, theory to guide simulator experiments, and analytical/computational frameworks tied to quantum simulation platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Concentration Area: experimental quantum simulation techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Experimental quantum simulation techniques and platforms to explore materials properties and behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should describe experimental platforms, how they will emulate target materials properties, and plan for non-equilibrium or hard-to-model regimes (mechanical, thermal, vibrational).

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Concentration Area: theoretical tools to extract properties from simulators
rubrics_metrics.description: Theoretical tools for understanding and extracting the materials properties from quantum simulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include algorithms, measurement protocols, and analysis methods to map simulator outputs to physical materials properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Concentration Area: materials fabrication and characterization for benchmarking
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials fabrication and characterization techniques for benchmarking simulation results and realizing new materials designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should include benchmark experiments or characterization methods to validate simulator predictions against real materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Concentration Area: incorporate simulator insights into computational materials science
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporating insights and data from quantum simulators into computational materials science techniques to improve fidelity, functionality, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect proposals to show how simulator-derived data improves or augments existing computational methods (e.g., DFT, MD).

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated Resources: quantum-simulator materials topic
rubrics_metrics.description: It is anticipated that awards under this topic will be no more than an average of $1.5M per year for up to 5 years, supporting no more than 6 funded faculty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget/team-size constraints should be respected unless exceptions are discussed with topic chiefs during white paper phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective: explore fundamental and practical limits in distributed entangled sensing
rubrics_metrics.description: The objective of this topic is to explore the fundamental and practical limits in distributed sensing that leverages the distribution of entanglement in a quantum network, including an analysis of the type of quantum state (e.g., continuous variable/discrete variable/hybrid configurations), network topology and signal processing approach needed to reach that limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should address information-theoretic limits, resilience to loss/decoherence, resources accounting, network topologies, and signal processing requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Concentration Area: novel modalities for distributed entanglement
rubrics_metrics.description: Novel modalities for the use of distributed entanglement in continuous, discrete and hybrid variable states in a network of sensors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include design/use of different quantum-state modalities and hybrid approaches for distributed sensing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Concentration Area: study fundamental limits of performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Study of the fundamental limits of performance of a distributed entangled sensing network (e.g. Is there any advantage beyond the known Heisenberg-scale sensitivity? Can quantum resources other than entanglement (e.g. non-locality) be leveraged?).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theoretical and experimental analysis of scaling laws, alternative quantum resources, and comparative metrics with single-apparatus limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Concentration Area: analyze network topologies and characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysis of advantages and challenges of different network topologies and characteristics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate how topology (connectivity, node heterogeneity) affects sensing performance and robustness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Concentration Area: signal processing for distributed sensors
rubrics_metrics.description: Exploration of signal processing techniques needed to combine the signals from the different sensors (including how to combine signals from disparate sensors and make the system resilient to node corruption).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include algorithms for fusion, fault/tamper resilience, and handling heterogeneous sensor modalities and noise models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated Resources: distributed entangled sensing topic
rubrics_metrics.description: It is anticipated that awards under this topic will be no more than an average of $1.5M per year for 5 years, supporting no more than 5 funded faculty researchers. Exceptions warranted by specific proposal approaches should be discussed with the topic chief during the white paper phase of the solicitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the stated resource envelope when planning team size and scope; discuss exceptions early with topic chief.

rubrics_metrics.name: HBCU/MI participation incentive (Topic 17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for Topic 17 are invited that include participation from eligible HBCUs/MIs; Applications with an HBCU/MI MURI team member may be eligible for $1.5M in total additional funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including eligible HBCU/MSI partners can enable access to additional funding — teams should consult Section I and topic chief during white paper phase for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective: develop architectures for perception using Foundation Models
rubrics_metrics.description: The goal is to develop architectures for understanding complex, dynamic environments from multi-modal data, with particular emphasis on inferring activities and causal models. Objectives include investigating and designing conceptual and computational frameworks for exploiting Foundation Models for understanding complex, dynamic environments, developing rigorous mathematical methods for evaluation and predicting performance, and investigating how to deal with shortcomings of FMs for reliable safe use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should address FM shortcomings (incorrect responses, logical inconsistencies), grounding in 4D space-time, and rigorous evaluation methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Concentration Area: architectures for incorporating Foundation Models
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigate and design principled architectures and computational methods for incorporating Foundation Models (FMs) for solving the inverse problem of perception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include architectures that combine FMs with neural-symbolic, generative, or simulation-based approaches for multi-step high-level perception tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Concentration Area: methods to detect/correct FM inaccuracies
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop rigorous methods to deal with inaccurate information that FMs may generate, and methods for detecting their potential internal logical inconsistencies and how to prevent and correct them. Also, investigate methods for improving the inference capabilities of FMs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should include detection mechanisms, correction strategies, robustness analyses, and improvements for safety-critical deployments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Concentration Area: distillation and deployment of FMs
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigate how the information contained in FMs can be distilled for particular application scenarios, and how FMs can be reduced for deployment on small mobile platforms and what the performance loss may be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address model compression, distillation, modality alignment, and tradeoffs for mobile/edge deployment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Concentration Area: mathematical methods to predict performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop rigorous mathematical methods to predict the performance of perception systems that incorporate FMs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These methods should complement empirical evaluation and target corner cases and theoretically-grounded performance bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated Resources: foundation models for perception topic
rubrics_metrics.description: It is anticipated that awards under this topic will be no more than an average of $1.5M per year for 5 years, supporting at most 8 funded faculty researchers. Exceptions warranted by specific proposal approaches should be discussed with topic chiefs during the white paper phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan team composition and scope to match stated funding and faculty support expectations; discuss exceptions early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective: develop quantitative gravity-wave coupling representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a quantitative numerical representation of lower atmosphere gravity wave coupling through mesospheric-ionospheric fate modeling that is underpinned by the theoretical models while matching the current observationally based empirical models from generation, propagation, and dissipation in the thermosphere-ionosphere, leading to improved numerical representation and prediction of ionospheric structure beyond diurnal solar forcing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should integrate theory, observations, and modeling across scales to improve prediction of ionospheric structure and variability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Concentration Area: sources, occurrences, and climatology of gravity-wave generation
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification and characterization of sources, occurrences, and climatology of non-orographic tropospheric gravity wave generation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include observational, diagnostic, and statistical analyses to quantify drivers and occurrence patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Concentration Area: mechanics of propagation and coupling
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanics of neutral atmosphere gravity wave propagation, coupling into the mesosphere and evolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work should address physical mechanisms controlling propagation, breaking, and energy/momentum deposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Concentration Area: effects on charged particle distributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Sensible effects of gravity waves on charged particle distribution and evolution in the ionosphere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate how neutral-atmosphere processes couple to ionospheric dynamics, chemistry, and impacts on DoD-relevant systems (communications, GPS).

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated Resources: gravity-wave/ionosphere topic
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards under this topic will be no more than $1.5M per year for 5 years, supporting no more than five funded faculty researchers. Exceptions warranted by specific proposal approaches may be discussed during the white paper phase of the solicitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use resource limits to size team and scope; consult topic chiefs for exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective: create and validate coastal permafrost erosion model
rubrics_metrics.description: This MURI will support a multidisciplinary team to create and validate through observations a comprehensive coastal erosion model for permafrost systems. The work will include a comprehensive study and understanding of local-regional scale variations in coastal permafrost that accounts for spatial and temporal variability of degradation and erosion, including thermoerosional & block failure mechanisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should couple observations and modeling to capture thermal-mechanical processes and offshore submarine permafrost evolution, and address sediment and carbon flux impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Concentration Area (required expertise): coastal wave modeling & permafrost erosion
rubrics_metrics.description: Research teams must incorporate the expertise needed for creation of a state-of-the-art, comprehensive coastal ocean model/module for thermal-mechanical permafrost erosion. Research concentration areas must include expertise in coastal wave modeling and permafrost erosion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals lacking core expertise in both coastal wave dynamics and permafrost erosion are unlikely to be competitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Concentration Area (suggested): Arctic oceanography, sea ice, cryohydrogeology, remote sensing
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional suggested research areas include but are not limited to Arctic oceanography & meteorology, sea ice dynamics, cryohydrogeology & geomorphology, and coastal remote sensing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These complementary disciplines are encouraged to form multidisciplinary teams to capture coupled system behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated Resources: coastal processes & permafrost topic
rubrics_metrics.description: It is anticipated that awards under this topic will be no more than an average of $1.5M per year for 5 years, supporting no more than five (5) funded faculty researchers. Exceptions warranted by specific proposal approaches should be discussed with the topic chiefs during the white paper phase of the solicitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget and team-size expectations guide scope and multi-institutional partnerships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective: increase fundamental knowledge of turbulent flow–soft fouling–compliant surfaces
rubrics_metrics.description: The objective is to increase our fundamental knowledge of the triadic interactions between turbulent boundary layer flow, soft fouling biology and compliant surfaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should aim for fundamental mechanistic understanding with potential implications for coatings, sensors, and drag/noise impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration expectation: multidisciplinary team for biofouling/turbulence research
rubrics_metrics.description: This MURI would benefit from collaboration between different fields, including marine and synthetic biology, biomechanics, fluid and solid mechanics, material science and hydroacoustics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teams should be multidisciplinary and include expertise spanning biology, mechanics, materials, and acoustics to address interactive phenomena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Concentration Area (i): influence of surface topology on fouling
rubrics_metrics.description: Influence of biotic and abiotic surface topology on fouling mechanisms, structures, and rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include experiments and modeling to relate surface texture/properties to settlement and growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Concentration Area (ii): dependence of fouling on environment & material properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Dependence of fouling mechanisms and growth on environmental factors and material surface properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address environmental conditioning, flow conditions, chemistry, and material interactions that modulate fouling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Concentration Area (iii): biomechanical properties of soft fouling/biofilms
rubrics_metrics.description: Biomechanical properties of SF and BF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure mechanical, structural, and adhesive properties and relate to flow-induced stresses and attachment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Concentration Area (iv): interaction of TBL flow, fouling organisms, wall vibrations, and impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Interaction between the TBL flow, fouling organisms, flow-induced wall vibrations, and resultant impact on drag, flow noise, fouling and coating adhesion response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine high-resolution flow diagnostics, structure sensing, and biological assays to quantify coupled effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model system focus: single organism cultures over rigid/elastic surfaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Research can focus on a model system comprised of single organism cultures of BF and/or filamentous algae (examples include but are not restricted to: Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Cellulophaga lytica, and Ulva linza) over rigid and elastomeric surfaces in high Re (turbulent) biofouling flow loops or channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using tractable model organisms/systems is acceptable as long as relevance to high-Re marine biofouling is justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated Resources: turbulent flow & fouling topic
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards under this topic will not exceed an average of $1.5M/year for 5 years, supporting six faculty researchers. Exceptions should be discussed with the topic chiefs during the white paper phase of the solicitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan teams and milestones to fit within the funding envelope; consult topic chiefs regarding exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: HBCU/MI participation incentive (Topic 21)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for Topic 21 are invited that include participation from eligible HBCUs/MIs; Applications with an HBCU/MI MURI team member may be eligible for $1.5M in total additional funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusion of eligible HBCU/MSI partners can unlock extra funds; consult solicitation Section I and topic chiefs for rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective: mechanistic understanding of template grain growth for POMS
rubrics_metrics.description: To develop mechanistic understanding of the template grain growth process for achieving controlled macroscale symmetry and to establish rational design strategies to efficiently explore the compositional and crystallographic spaces for desired physical properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should couple theory, in-situ characterization, computational techniques, and demonstrations of device concepts leveraging organized macro-symmetry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Concentration Area (1): diffusion and transport in multi-element environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Diffusion and transport phenomena in a multi-element environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study kinetics and transport processes during grain growth in complex chemistries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Concentration Area (2): phase stability and chemical compatibility criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishment of phase stability and chemical compatibility criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define phase diagrams, stability windows, and compatibility constraints for templated growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Concentration Area (3): seeding strategy (composition, morphology, symmetry, pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Seeding strategy including composition, morphology, symmetry, pattern, and associated crystal chemistry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate how seed choice and patterning controls macro-symmetry and properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Concentration Area (4): in-situ characterization of template grain growth
rubrics_metrics.description: In-situ characterization of the template grain growth process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use experimental in-situ probes to capture dynamics of grain growth and microstructure evolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Concentration Area (5): origin of dielectric and mechanical losses
rubrics_metrics.description: Origin of dielectric and mechanical losses under high electric field and high stresses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link microstructure, domain behavior, and loss mechanisms to high-drive performance limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Concentration Area (6): computational techniques to facilitate design and prediction
rubrics_metrics.description: Computational techniques that facilitate material design and prediction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop modeling tools that guide composition and symmetry design and predict properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Concentration Area (7): novel concepts for multiscale symmetry
rubrics_metrics.description: Novel concepts for multiscale symmetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explore additive manufacturing, metamaterials, and multiscale templating to create new macroscale symmetries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Concentration Area (8): demonstration of unique transducer design using organized macro-symmetry
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstration of unique transducer design using organized macro-symmetry concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate materials advances into transducer or device demonstrations that highlight advantages of POMS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated Resources: POMS topic
rubrics_metrics.description: It is anticipated that awards under this topic will be no more than $1.5M per year for 5 years, supporting 5-7 faculty researchers. Exceptions warranted by specific proposal approaches should be discussed with the topic chiefs during the white paper phase of the solicitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use funding/team-size guidance to scope experiments, in-situ campaigns, and device demonstrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective: measure, model, and manipulate variability in judgments/decision making
rubrics_metrics.description: The objective of this topic is to gain a deepened understanding of measuring, modeling, and manipulating the variability in judgments and decision making. This understanding should lead to the development of experimentally validated techniques for identifying candidates for highly variable judgments/decisions as well as the measurement, computational modeling, and manipulation of that variability to improve decision making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize experimentally causal approaches (manipulations) and generalizable computational models relevant to operational/DoD tasks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Concentration Area: multidisciplinary expertise for experiments and modeling
rubrics_metrics.description: The envisioned research requires multidisciplinary expertise in areas such as organizational psychology, social and behavioral sciences, mathematics, computer science/AI, and human-computer interaction in order to design and conduct basic research experiments; extract, analyze and interpret data; create and validate predictive computational models of the mechanisms underlying the variability and its impacts on performance; and institute systematic approaches for model and manipulation validation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teams should combine experimentalists and modelers to enable causal inference and model validation across contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Expectation: minimally intrusive measurement techniques and scaling methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals are sought for minimally intrusive techniques to measure decision making noise in cases where variability is undesirable, create and empirically validate computational models of the mechanisms underlying noise generation in decision making, and propose and experimentally test manipulations of variability that can exert an impact on performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Techniques should be applicable in realistic/naturalistic settings with plan to scale to more complex decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive Proposal Deliverable (1): identify candidates and quantify activities in naturalistic settings
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods of identifying candidates for highly variable decisions/judgements as well as capturing and quantifying activities, decisions, and performance in naturalistic settings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include procedures and metrics to detect high-noise decision contexts and quantify variability at individual and group levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive Proposal Deliverable (2): predictive computational modeling of variability mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Predictive computational modeling of the processes underlying the modulation of variability in decisions and the impacts of this variability on decision making processes and performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Models should be validated experimentally and explain mechanisms that generate noise and how they influence outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive Proposal Deliverable (3): techniques and experiments to manipulate variability
rubrics_metrics.description: Techniques, experimental conditions, and hypotheses for manipulating variability within socio-technical systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and test interventions (procedural, interface, training, algorithmic) that reduce unwanted variability without impairing adaptability where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive Proposal Deliverable (4): empirically validated evaluation and generalization approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Empirically validated approaches for evaluating and generalizing the models across multiple use cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide plans to generalize models across domains (e.g., sonar, imagery, navigation) and scale up to more complex decision tasks.
